latest.question: Deputy Naoise Ó Muirí asked the Minister for Health the status of the proposed redevelopment of Beaumont Hospital’s emergency department.
latest.reply:
There are a number of significant proposals for capital investment in Beaumont. These projects must be carefully sequenced to protect clinical activity while delivering the greatest benefit for patients.
The hospital has identified a clear order of priority. The first project is a major extension to the Radiation Oncology Centre. Enabling works are well under way, with main construction expected to commence in 2027.
This will be followed by a new inpatient bed block, which received planning permission in 2024. The additional beds will increase capacity and help relieve pressure on the Emergency Department. The proposed new permanent Emergency Department will follow the bed block.
The proposed new Emergency Department at Beaumont Hospital received a final grant of planning in May 2025. The project is progressing through the detailed design stage at present. That detailed design will inform a tender and market engagement strategy for construction works that will determine construction timelines.
In the short term, additional emergency capacity will be provided through a two-storey modular extension beside the existing department. This will expand reception and waiting areas, relocate support services, free up clinical space, improve patient pathways and reduce congestion.
The main Contractor has been appointed, with site mobilisation and construction commencement now underway.

latest.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Health the measures being taken to address the challenges facing patients presenting to hospital emergency departments with mental health difficulties, particularly lengthy waiting times for psychiatric assessments and access to appropriate care.
latest.reply:
Emergency departments are not the most appropriate environment for people experiencing a mental health crisis. That is why I, as Minister for Mental Health, have prioritised the development and rollout of community-based alternatives that provide earlier intervention, more appropriate support, and reduce the need for people to present to emergency departments.
The reality is that the prevalence of mental health challenges is increasing and the complexity of cases is also growing. As demand rises, Government recognises the need to ensure people in crisis can access specialist supports in settings that are better suited to their needs.
In response, I have consistently enabled the development of new crisis services and innovative Models of Care designed to provide timely, intensive support outside of hospital settings, in tandem with those supports in emergency departments.
For example, the National Clinical Programme for Self-harm and Suicide-related Ideation (NCPSHI) was first introduced in Irish public hospital emergency departments in 2014 and continues to articulate the standards of care in this regard. The Programme is primarily delivered by clinical nurse specialists with support from a consultant psychiatrist in each hospital area.

latest.question: Deputy Barry Ward asked the Minister for Health the position regarding any initiatives proposed by her Department to further support breastfeeding mothers including but not limited to increasing the provision of lactation consultants employed by the HSE.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 59 and 96 together.
Encouraging mothers to breastfeed is a priority, both for the Department of Health and for the HSE. Breastfeeding as a public health measure is protective against Non - Communicable Diseases and is the optimum nutrition for infants.
There has been considerable progress under the HSE Breastfeeding in a Healthy Ireland 2016-2025 Action Plan, resulting in a modest 7% increase in breastfeeding rates. However, further cultural and societal change is required to support breastfeeding in Ireland. The Government allocated funding in budget 2026 to increasing lactation consultants , of which staffing levels have increased fourfold over the last several years.
In 2025, the Department of Health formed a breastfeeding steering group to research and design the development of a new whole of government breastfeeding strategy.
Over the last year, the Department of Health has engaged with multiple stakeholders and across government, to inform how the new strategy will be designed.
A large multistakeholder event was held in November 2025, followed by specific focus groups in January 2026. A final workshop focusing on stakeholder implementation was hosted by the department in February. The consultation report has been published on the healthy Ireland website.

latest.question: Deputy David Cullinane asked the Minister for Health her plans to improve access to services for HIV, eliminate new transmissions, and reduce waiting times for PrEP.
latest.reply:
Sexual health is a priority for the Department of Health.
The National Sexual Health Strategy (NSHS), 2025-2035 was published in 2025. The NSHS is supported by the National Sexual Health Action Plan, 2025-2028, the first of 3 Action Plans under the NSHS, which maps out the first 3 years of delivery in more detail.
The NSHS includes a number of priorities directly related to HIV:
• Developing an Action Plan to support elimination of new HIV transmissions by 2030, in line with international targets, also providing a Model of Care and additional supports for people living with HIV. Work on this has commenced.
• Increasing the availability of HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) and reducing waiting times for access to it.
A number of additional priorities include HIV, in addition to other priorities in wider education, prevention and care measures:
• Extending the provision of information and educational resources to people of all ages, backgrounds and ethnicities. This includes HIV anti-stigma campaigns, such as You, Me and HIV
• Developing a comprehensive Model of Care for Sexual Health to provide an equitable roadmap for sexual health service delivery and improvement.
• Widening access to equitable sexual health care, across our new Health Regions, with a clear focus on improving prevention, testing, surveillance, early diagnosis and treatment for STIs and HIV and supporting wider public health priorities.
• Widening and deepening the research base supporting sexual health pol

latest.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Health to report on the repairs of the MRI scanner in Connolly Hospital, Blanchardstown.
latest.reply:
The MRI scanner is maintained in accordance with the relevant manufacturer maintenance requirements and agreed Service Level Agreement (SLA). A routine service of the MRI scanner was commissioned on 4 November 2026. During this routine maintenance additional issues arose that extended the MRI downtime. The HSE have also advised that engineers remained on site each day, including over the weekend, to address these issues and in order to restore the scanner to clinical use as soon as possible.
I have been assured by the HSE that the MRI scanner in Connolly Hospital Blanchardstown returned to clinical use on the morning of 11 November.
In the interim, I have been advised that appropriate alternative care pathways were implemented to ensure continuity of patient care. Where clinically appropriate, arrangements were made to facilitate the transfer of patients to other hospitals or third-party radiology service providers for MRI examinations. Alternatively, other suitable diagnostic pathways were explored in accordance with individual patient needs and clinical judgement.

latest.question: Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health for an updated on the implementation of Smile agus Sláinte.
latest.reply:
My Department and the HSE are finalising a focused two-year Oral Health Action Plan to deliver real improvements for patients in accessing oral healthcare.
The plan will be driven by a dedicated governance group, with progress monitored closely and aligned to wider HSE and Department priorities. It will aim to respond to sustained service pressures and long waiting lists—particularly for children and for people with additional needs.
It will focus on a small number of clear priorities:
• Cutting waiting lists in the School Dental Programme and orthodontics
• Expanding the access programme for people with additional needs and disabilities
• Review of the Dental Treatment Services Scheme
• Support for recruitment, education and training
• Support for innovation and new ways of delivering care
Over the next two years, the aim is to stabilise services, reduce waiting times, and make access measurably better for patients—while laying the groundwork for longer-term reform. Budget 2027 provides €18 million to commence implementation of the Plan.
The longer term reform of oral healthcare services will be achieved through the National Oral Health Policy Smile agus Sláinte. latest.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Health the number of prospective HSE employees whose start dates are pending recruitment pay bill approval from her Department, if a hospital by hospital breakdown can be provided on that figure.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 8 and 9 together.
To start, I want to acknowledge the uncertainty and personal disruption that waiting for confirmation of a start date can cause for candidates and their families. Planning recruitment and seeking the necessary approvals early is important, and I expect the HSE to manage the process in a way that offers candidates greater certainty and assurance. Officials from my Department are working with colleagues in the HSE to support the preparation and submission of the necessary applications for approval.
To help address this, an expedited application process has been agreed with the HSE for posts where contractual commitments have been made. The HSE must identify the posts concerned and provide the necessary information so that applications can be considered promptly.
On the numbers awaiting approval, the position as of this morning is that my Department has received requests concerning contractually committed posts covering 53 WTE in Dublin and Midlands and one role in West and North West. The West and North West role has already been approved, with the Dublin and Midlands requests currently under review following consultation with the Region.
Separately, requests have been received for 554 WTE graduate nurse and midwife posts, all of which have now been approved. Of these, 93 were approved in Dublin and Midlands, 100 in Dublin and South East, 176.5 in the South West and 184.5 in the West and North West.

latest.question: Deputy Peter Roche asked the Minister for Health the steps her Department is taking to reduce waiting times for psychiatric assessments in County Galway in both child and adolescent mental health services and adult mental health services; and the measures being taken to improve the recruitment and retention of psychiatric and mental health staff.
latest.reply:
All aspects of mental health care are being enhanced in line with the implementation of our mental health policy Sharing the Vision 2020-2030 and our suicide reduction strategy Connecting for Life: 2026-2035.
Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services:
As the Deputy may be aware, I visited 21 CAMHS teams nationwide last year and met with the Regional Executive Officers and their staff to focus on improvements to all aspects of youth mental health care. I conveyed in my meeting with each Health Region that reducing the CAMHS waiting list is one of my main priorities.
As part of the process to address extended wait times for CAMHS, each Health Region has submitted a waitlist improvement plan inclusive of monthly targets to eliminate over 12-month waiters by the end of December 2026. All regions have committed to achieving this goal and have set out the specific measures being implemented locally to improve access, reduce wait times and support the delivery of the December 2026 target.
As of 31 August 2026, there were 317 young people waiting to access CAMHS across the Integrated Health Area of Galway and Roscommon. Significantly, no young person was waiting over 12 months to access care in Galway.

Emergency departments are not the most appropriate environment for people experiencing a mental health crisis. That is why I, as Minister for Mental Health, have prioritised the development and rollout of community-based alternatives that provide earlier intervention, more appropriate support, and reduce the need for people to present to emergency departments.

• The introduction of 2 new Crisis Resolution Teams in Wexford and North Tipperary.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
